answer: Receiving-end voltage exceeds sending-end voltage at no load
author: Hermes
options: Receiving-end voltage exceeds sending-end voltage at no load
Line current is zero at no load
Active power flows from receiving to sending end
The line behaves as a pure resistor
question: A long EHV transmission line is energised at no load. What is the Ferranti effect?
solution: The line capacitance draws charging current, which causes a voltage rise along the line, so the receiving-end voltage exceeds the sending-end voltage at no (or light) load. Topic (transmission lines) is in the Power Systems section of the official GATE 2027 EE syllabus. Source checked: https://gate2027.iitm.ac.in/static/doc/GATE2027_Syllabus/EE_GATE2027_Syllabus.pdf
